review_notes: I reviewed all of OriginalBlock78.lean. It has two data definitions, a `decide +kernel` certificate check, and one evaluation theorem. I grepped the sibling files. The evaluation theorem is stamped out once per block (91 OriginalBlock*.lean files), for example originalBlockEval77, originalBlockEval79 and originalBlockEval0. Each proof is the same three-step rewrite: `rw [originalBlockCheckN, Integer.Sparse.eval_collectBalanced, Integer.Sparse.eval_substitute]`. The reasoning is already factored into the general lemmas `Integer.Sparse.eval_collectBalanced` (CompareMerge.lean) and `Integer.Sparse.eval_substitute` (MixedTargetBasic.lean). A shared helper of the form `blk = collectBalanced … → eval blk x = …` would only wrap those two lemmas around a hypothesis. That is a thin wrapper around existing API and a short routine rewrite, so it is not nontrivial repeated proof machinery. The check theorem is a kernel `decide` on block-specific data, so there is no shared argument to extract. I did not read the full definitions of the Sparse API. Neither did I look at the uses in OriginalMerge*.lean beyond the call sites shown by grep.
